subject: Post-call recap & pilot kickoff: success metrics, prompt suite, and next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlasai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T14:12:00Z
Subject: Quick recap and proposed pilot scope (next steps)

Alex — thanks for taking time today. Short recap from my side and ask for alignment so we can get the pilot moving this week.

Key pain you described:
- High variability in response latency when routing customer queries to existing LLM endpoints (spikes during peak traffic).
- Unit cost is growing disproportionately as you scale (esp. for re-ranking + embeddings workflows).
- Need deterministic behavior for certain customer-facing flows (fraud alerts / policy checks).

Goals you called out:
1) Reduce tail latency (95th/99th) for the QA and notification workflows to sub-400ms where possible.
2) Cut per-conversation token spend by ~30% via batching + prefix caching without regressing on accuracy.
3) Establish a reproducible prompt/eval suite so product and data science can measure regressions.

Proposed pilot scope (30 days):
- Model + infra: Redwood hosted inference using quantized variant (rwd-3-small-q4) for re-rank & embed, rwd-3-medium for fidelity-sensitive QA.
- Success metrics: 95th latency, average cost per session, and accuracy on a 150-example prompt set (A/B vs your baseline).
- Deliverables: prompt suite (spreadsheet), synthetic load-run, latency/cost dashboard access, a one-page runbook for failover.
- Owners: Tessa (Sales/Eng. sponsor), Ben (Solutions/onsite engineer), Atlas lead: Alex (product).
- Access needed: API key whitelist, sample logs (anonymized) for traffic profile, S3 read access to a small dataset for prompt examples.

Attachments: sow-draft-v1.pdf (starter SOW), pilot-prompt-suite-sample.xlsx (example prompts & eval format).

Next steps: can you confirm the access items above and whether 5/3 or 5/6 works to schedule a 30–45m kickoff? Also: are there any procurement constraints we should loop in now?

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlasai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap and proposed pilot scope (next steps)

Tessa — thanks for the clear notes. This matches how we saw the call. A few clarifications and answers: 

- Access: procurement can approve a scoped S3 read role and an API allowlist for a single test key for the pilot. I copied them to start the SOW/PO discussion.
- Timeline: 5/3 is tight for us (leadership review), 5/6 looks good for a kickoff.
- Success metrics: the team prefers defining accuracy as "no more than 3% regression on our labeled NLU set" rather than an absolute threshold. We'll share the labeled set (anonymized).
- Security: we need a brief note about data retention (30 days max, logs only) and whether keys can be rotated automatically.

I'll bring in procurement to confirm any required paperwork. For the prompt set: we'll upload examples to the Drive link you provided once you confirm the kickoff time.

— Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Product, Atlas AI

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlasai.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T16:20:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap and proposed pilot scope — prep items for kickoff (5/6)

Ben / Grace — forwarding Alex's confirmation. We're set to kickoff on 2027-05-06 at 10:00 PT pending procurement sign-off. Please see the ask below and let me know if you need anything prepped.

Action items (owner):
- Ben: prepare a lightweight load profile runbook and small synthetic workload we can run against Atlas's test key (goal: reproduce 95/99 latency under representative burst).
- Grace: assemble the prompt/eval spreadsheet into Redwood's eval runner format and create an initial scoring rubric (accuracy/regression thresholds).
- Tessa: finalize SOW and share an initial DocuSign link for signature; confirm API allowlist process and key rotation docs for Atlas security.

Procurement — attaching the starter SOW (sow-draft-v1.pdf). Happy to adjust scope if the PO needs a line-item for dedicated capacity; current proposal assumes shared hosted with agreed SLOs for the pilot window.

Attachment stub: sow-draft-v1.pdf (1.2 MB) — draft SOW: scope, timeline, estimated token budget.

Quoted:

Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlasai.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap and proposed pilot scope — prep items for kickoff (5/6)

All — I'll own the synthetic load and plan to ship a simple harness by EOD 5/3. Initial plan: two profiles (burst/steady) matching the sample logs Alex will upload. For the pilot we'll benchmark:
- 50 concurrent sessions (burst) for 10s windows
- steady 5 req/s sustained for 30m
I'll include a runbook section describing how to toggle prefix caching and a recommended quantization profile for Atlas's model shapes.

Prompt suite: Grace, if you can take the sample spreadsheet and add a column for expected output and tolerance, I can wire the harness to drive the eval runner.

Attachments: pilot-prompt-suite-sample.xlsx (0.4 MB)

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
